title: Bina and tevuna: grasping a concept and drawing it out

provenance.note: Ported from the demo's Markdown. Three things are coarser than a file written for this format: the phrases are whole paragraphs of Rabbi Markel's published translation (Sefaria, "The Gate of Unity", 2023, CC-BY), not phrases as translated in class; each block's word range starts where the demo's listen link pointed and its end is estimated (up to the next cited point, at most about 450 words); and the demo's style left out banter, stories and digressions, which `yarn study-check` lists as uncited stretches.

overview: The first chapter dealt with *bina*, the analysis and understanding of a concept. This chapter shows that *bina* has two levels: *bina* itself and *tevuna*, the light of *bina* spreading forth. *Tevuna* comes from *kelita*, absorbing a matter by going over it again even after it is understood. The man of *bina* goes down into the deep well and drinks there; the man of *tevuna* brings the water up to the sheep. Without *tevuna* a person can understand a Talmudic debate perfectly and still be unable to rule on it, and whole societies can think great thoughts that never come to anything. *Tevuna* is the lower mother: it turns the emotions within *bina* into real emotions of the heart, through *daas*. *Hisbonenus*, *bina sheb'bina*, joins the two, and that is why contemplation is a service of G-d and not only an intellectual exercise.

terms.gloss: understanding; going down into a concept and analyzing it

a man of tevuna; one who can draw the deep waters up to others

sections.title: Tevuna: the light of bina spreading forth
sections.summary: Bina has two levels, bina and tevuna. Tevuna is the light of bina spreading forth, and it comes when a concept is absorbed by going over it again even after it is understood.

phrases.he: (ב) והנה ידוע שיש בבינה עצמה ב' מדרגות, בינה ותבונה, וענין התבונה הוא בחינת התפשטות אור הבינה (כמו שכתוב בזהר דאבא ואמא תתאין הם ישראל סבא ותבונה, ונקרא אימא תתאה כו')
phrases.en: Now, it is known that in *Binah* itself there are two levels; *Binah* and *Tvunah*. The matter of *Tvunah* is the aspect of the spreading forth of the light of *Binah.* (This is as stated in the Zohar, “The lower mother and father are *Yisroel Saba* and *Tvunah.*” ]*Tvunah* is[ called the lower mother.)
notes: See Zohar Ha’azinu 290b and 291a. See also Etz Chayim (Shaar Av”I) Shaar 21, chapter 8.

blocks.text: **Now, it is known that in *Binah* itself there are two levels; *Binah* and *Tvunah*.**

*Bina* (understanding), as discussed in the first chapter, basically means analysis. **The matter of *Tvunah* is the aspect of the spreading forth of the light of *Binah*.** The definition continues after the parenthesis, in the next line: the light spreads forth because the concept is grasped well in the receiving vessel. The parenthesis brings the Zohar, where *tevuna* is **called the lower mother** (*Ima tata'a*).

phrases.he: מצד קליטתה היטב בכלי המקבל ההשגה דבינה, על כן מתפשט בה להביאה בכמה ענינים נבדלים מעצם ההשגה, והוא הנקרא איש תבונה, כמו מים עמוקים כו' איש תבונה ידלנה.
phrases.en: ]This comes about[ because ]the concept[ is grasped very well in the vessel of the comprehension of *Binah*. Therefore, [through this], it spreads forth to bring it into many matters that are separate from the essential comprehension ]of the concept itself[. ]One who is capable of[ this is called “a man of *Tvunah*,” as in ]the verse], “Deep waters… a man of *Tevunah* shall draw them out.”

blocks.text: The light of *bina* spreads forth because the concept **is grasped very well in the vessel of the comprehension of *Binah***.
This too comes specifically from *hisbonenus* (contemplation), from going over the matter again and again.

When one contemplates a matter until it is understood well and stops there, he has *bina*, but not *tevuna*. If he keeps going over it even after he understands it well, it is absorbed into the receiving vessel of the comprehension, into his brain. Then **it spreads forth to bring it into many matters that are separate from the essential comprehension**: it can go out into various things that are separate from the understanding itself.

One who can do this is called **“a man of *Tvunah*,”** the one who can **draw them out**, the deep waters.

Understanding a matter well gives *bina*. *Kelita* (absorption), and with it *tevuna*, comes from going over it again after it is already understood.

phrases.he: מים עמוקים הם בחינת עמקות בינה שנשאר בהעלם העצמיות, ואיש תבונה דווקא ידלנה וישאבנה מן ההעלם להביאה להתפשטות בכמה אופנים שונים לרוות את המקבלים
phrases.en: The “deep waters” represent the aspect of the depths of *Binah* which remain concealed in the essential self. It is specifically the “man of *Tvunah*” who draws it out and brings it forth from its concealment, to bring it to spread forth in many different manners, in order to quench the thirst of the recipients.

blocks.text: **The “deep waters” represent the aspect of the depths of *Binah* which remain concealed in the essential self.**
The real depth of a concept stays concealed within the concept itself, as with the matters studied in this very book.

This book is always a *mashal* (analogy) on itself. Here the Mitteler Rebbe is the man of *tevuna*: specifically he **draws it out and brings it forth from its concealment, to bring it to spread forth in many different manners, in order to quench the thirst of the recipients**, and the recipients are us.

sections.title: Drawing up deep waters: bina goes down, tevuna brings up
sections.summary: The man of bina goes down into the well and drinks there; the man of tevuna brings the water up to the sheep. Tevuna spreads forth from bina and brings its depth down to others, so as a pair bina is the width and tevuna the length.

phrases.he: כמו הדולה מים עמוקים להשקות הצאן כו' והוא כמו שאנו רואים בחוש, שבהיות השכל והסברא עמוקים ביותר מהכיל בהשגת אדם, הנקרא מים עמוקים כו', שהוא בחינת עומק המושג הנזכר לעיל שהאורך והרוחב ממנו בא כו'
phrases.en: This is analogous to one who draws out deep waters to quench the thirst of the sheep. We may clearly observe that when the reasoning of a concept is too deep to be retained in the comprehension of man, this is called “deep waters,” which is the aspect of the depth of the comprehension (*Omek HaMoosag*), from which the length and width come, as previously explained.

blocks.text: **This is analogous to one who draws out deep waters to quench the thirst of the sheep.**

blocks.title: Watering the sheep from a deep well
blocks.text: There are two ways to give the sheep water from a deep well. One can throw each sheep into the well and pull it out again, or one can take the water out and bring it up to the sheep.

First there has to be a man of *bina*. He goes deep into the well itself; he does not bring the water out. He can drink because he is all the way down at the level of the water, in the depths, but that does not help the sheep. The man of *tevuna* takes that water and brings it from deep water to shallow water.

So **when the reasoning of a concept is too deep to be retained in the comprehension of man, this is called “deep waters,”** and again this book is itself the example: it speaks of very deep matters, the deep waters of the *taalumos chachma* (hidden depths of wisdom). A well is dug down to the aquifer, and the water stays down in the aquifer. That is **the depth of the comprehension (*Omek HaMoosag*), from which the length and width come**.

phrases.he: ואיש בעל תבונה דווקא ידלנה, פירוש שיוציא לאור בחינת העלם העומק המושג עד שיכילנו השגת האדם, כאלו לא היה עמוק כלל, כמו הדולה מים עמוקים שמקרב את העומק כו'
phrases.en: It is specifically one who possesses the power of *Tvunah* who can “draw it out.” In other words, he brings to light the aspect of the hidden depth of the concept, until it may be retained within the comprehension of man, as if it was not deep at all. Just as [in the analogy of] one who draws the deep waters [out of the depths of the well], he brings the depth [itself] close.

blocks.text: **It is specifically one who possesses the power of *Tvunah* who can “draw it out.”**

Here the Mitteler Rebbe draws it up, like the pail drawing water from a well. In other words, **he brings to light the aspect of the hidden depth of the concept, until it may be retained within the comprehension of man, as if it was not deep at all**, so that a regular person without such a deep mind, like us, can hold it.

Even earlier generations with very great minds could not go into this depth, and here we are receiving it. Why? Because the man of *tevuna* brought it out to our level, the way water is brought from the aquifer to the sheep.
It is deep by any standard, yet a regular college student, with a little explanation, could learn it.
Like one who draws water from the well, **he brings the depth [itself] close** to the sheep.

phrases.he: ולפי זה מוכרח לומר שכח התבונה הוא כח המתפשט מכח הבינה להביא עומקה לגילוי למטה למקבלים כו'
phrases.en: According to the above, we must say that the power of *Tvunah* is a power that spreads forth from the power of *Binah*, to bring its depth into revelation below to the recipients.

blocks.text: One must say that **the power of *Tvunah* is a power that spreads forth from the power of *Binah***.

It is not the power of *bina* itself. The power of *bina* does not draw the water out of the aquifer; it goes down into the aquifer, like a man with a drill who must himself go down into the depth in order to drink.

The power of *tevuna* spreads out from the power of *bina*: without the understanding into the thing, one cannot bring it out. It depends on having the power of *bina* first, **to bring its depth into revelation below to the recipients**.
Of the two, *bina* and *tevuna*, *tevuna* is the *orech* (length).

The length of *bina* is the power to explain the matter to oneself; the length of *tevuna* is the power to explain it to somebody else. Each of them has its own width and length, but as a pair *tevuna* is the length and *bina* is the *rochav* (width): *bina* spreads out into all the different parts. Compared to *chachma*, *chachma* is called the width and *bina* the length; within *bina*, *bina* is the width and *tevuna* the length.

sections.title: The tafsan: a fine grasp that stays where it is
sections.summary: A person can be strong in bina, a good grasper, and still nothing comes out of his understanding: no application and no explanation to anyone else. Whole societies can be like this.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כשאינו איש תבונות, גם שהוא בעל השגה במוח דבינה (שנקרא תפסן בלשון העולם) יוכל להיות שהשגתו נשארת רק כמו שהיא בעצם, במוח הבינה שלו שנקרא רוח בינתו לבד, ולא יבוא ממנה שום התפשטות למטה בענין נבדל שחוץ מן עצם ההשגה כלל
phrases.en: This is not the case with one who is not “a man of *Tvunah*.” Although he may be a man of comprehension in his mind of *Binah*, (which is called a “*Tafsan* –Grasper” in the terminology of the world,) it is possible that his comprehension remains as it is in the essence of his mind of *Binah*. ]That is, he only possesses[ “the spirit of *Binah*,” but there will not come from it any spreading down into separate matters, outside of the essential comprehension itself.

blocks.text: **This is not the case with one who is not “a man of *Tvunah*.”**

He may be **a man of comprehension in his mind of *Binah*** (a *tafsan*, a “grabber,” who has a good grip on the matter): a person with *bina*, but not so much *tevuna*. Then **it is possible that his comprehension remains as it is in the essence of his mind of *Binah***: he understands it, but his understanding stays just the way it is. He can drink the water because he went down into the depth.
Yet **there will not come from it any spreading down into separate matters, outside of the essential comprehension itself**: no application, and no explanation to anyone else.

blocks.title: The Greeks and the Americans
blocks.text: Societies show this too: the Greeks and the Americans. The Greek power was *bina*; the American, and the whole modern Western, power is specifically *tevuna*: not so much understanders as appliers.

blocks.title: The Greeks' steam turbine
blocks.text: The Greeks had a working steam turbine, knew about electricity, the wheel, metal, and oil from the ground that burns, and could have started the Industrial Revolution two thousand years ago. For them it was all pure intellect, the pursuit of intellect and not of the dollar, and they never thought of it on so low a level as application.
So a person, and even a whole society, can stay entirely within *bina* with no spreading forth from it at all, even though he may be a greater master of *bina* than the man of *tevuna*.

A Greek philosopher would have considered the Wright brothers or Edison crude people (*grobbe mentshen*), thinking about how to build a better horse carriage. Nonetheless a person can have more *tevuna* even though he does not have so much *bina*. And the advances of *tevuna* also come specifically from *bina sheb'bina* (bina within bina), from the analysis of the thing.

phrases.he: וגם שיש בהשגה אורך ורוחב ועומק כנזכר לעיל, הכל הוא רק בעצם ההשגה, כמו שהיא, אבל לא שיתגלה למטה בענין נבדל, ומכל שכן עומק המושג הרי נשאר בעומקו בהעלם לעצמו, וכן האורך והרוחב, הכל בעצם ההשגה כמו שהיא, שהיא במקומה לבד
phrases.en: Furthermore, although his comprehension is in the length, width and depth, as explained above, it is all in the essential comprehension, as it is. However, it will not be revealed below in separate matters, and certainly, the depth of the concept remains in its depth, concealed in itself. Likewise, the length and width all [remain] in the essential comprehension, as they are, in that state alone.

blocks.text: Furthermore, **although his comprehension is in the length, width and depth, as explained above, it is all in the essential comprehension, as it is.**
Even his explaining it “downward” is really to himself, not to others; to explain to somebody else is specifically the work of *tevuna*.
However, **it will not be revealed below in separate matters**, and revealing a thing in a separate matter is just what a *mashal* does.

All the more, **the depth of the concept remains in its depth, concealed in itself**, as with the Greek philosophers: nothing came out of it. Not only that, they did not even explain it to ordinary people. It was for a few of the elite, who were happy to think about these things and never thought to explain them to the man working in the marketplace. In America, by contrast, the whole idea is that everybody has to learn it and understand it.
**Likewise, the length and width all [remain] in the essential comprehension, as they are, in that state alone.**

sections.title: The Talmudic debate that yields no ruling
sections.summary: One can master every line of reasoning in a Talmudic debate and still be unable to rule guilty or innocent. That ability, to bring the concept down into a separate matter, a verdict, an emotion of the heart or many angles of thought, is the power of tevuna.

phrases.he: ודוגמא לכל זה, הנה אנו רואים בעומק הפלפול בתלמוד וטעמים בסברות רבות כך וכך
phrases.en: An example of all this can be seen in the depth of the logical debate of the Talmud, in which there are many reasons and explanations to argue one way or another etc.

phrases.he: גם שבאים בהשגה דבינה, אבל לא יוכלו עדיין להוציא לאור מעצם השכל איזה פסק דין חייב או זכאי כלל
phrases.en: Although one may come to the comprehension of *Binah,* nonetheless, he still is incapable of bringing to light any actual verdict or ruling of “innocent” or “guilty” from the essential intellect.

blocks.text: **An example of all this can be seen in the depth of the logical debate of the Talmud, in which there are many reasons and explanations to argue one way or another**.

Some people can master a whole *pilpul* (Talmudic debate) and understand all its *sevaros* (lines of reasoning), yet cannot apply it to anything: **he still is incapable of bringing to light any actual verdict or ruling of “innocent” or “guilty” from the essential intellect.**
In a way the power of *tevuna* has a higher root than the power of *bina*, because to bring a matter out one must understand it more deeply than the original understanding.

The Greek philosophers were in one way greater than the modern scientists, yet because the modern scientists applied the ideas, they came to understand the principles better than the Greeks did with their *bina*.

Even among the Greeks, the famous story of the clever Greek is about *tevuna*, not *bina*: Archimedes sat and thought and never tried to apply anything, until the king had a problem that needed an application. Because he had to apply it, he understood the thing more deeply, and so came the “eureka” and the principle of the displacement of water.
So someone may understand the Talmud, while the great *poskim* (halachic authorities), like the Rambam, could apply it to an actual ruling of guilty or innocent.

phrases.he: דהיינו שלא יוכל להוציא מתוך הסברה איזה חיוב על פי זה השכל ולא איזה זכות על פי זה השכל
phrases.en: In other words, one is not capable of bringing out any “guilty” verdict from this reasoning, nor any “innocent” verdict from this reasoning.

phrases.he: כי עדיין אין השכל והסברה רק השכלה שכליות לבד, בלתי ימצא ממנו שום התפשטות בהטיות לענין נבדל הימנה, שהוא לחייב על ידה או לזכות על ידה
phrases.en: This is because, as of yet, these concepts and explanations are only theoretical abstractions. One will, therefore, not find any spreading forth into matters which are separate from them. In other words, [he will not be capable] of applying these reasons and explanations [in practice] and state a “guilty” or an “innocent” verdict through them.

blocks.text: In other words, **one is not capable of bringing out any “guilty” verdict from this reasoning, nor any “innocent” verdict from this reasoning.**
One can learn the whole subject in the Talmud, but actually to rule on it he will not be able to do.
**This is because, as of yet, these concepts and explanations are only theoretical abstractions.**

To find guilty or innocent through them, to **state a “guilty” or an “innocent” verdict**, is the matter of *chesed* and *gevura* (kindness and severity), and *chesed* and *gevura* do not come out of *bina*; they come specifically from *tevuna*.

phrases.he: והרי זה כמו דבר ההיולי שלא נודע עדיין מה ימצא ממנה ומה יעשה בה (בל"א דער מושכל אליין כמו שהוא ער קאן מיט אים נישט טאן קיין זאך ניט צו קערין לזכות או לחוב כו')
phrases.en: Rather, it is like a *Heyulie* power, in which it is not yet known what will result from it or what could be done with it.

blocks.text: Rather, **it is like a *Heyulie* power, in which it is not yet known what will result from it or what could be done with it.**
It is just an idea, and nobody knows what will come out of it or what can be done with it.
The Yiddish line in the Hebrew text says it plainly: the concept by itself, as it is, one can do nothing with it, to lean (*noteh*) either to merit or to guilt.

phrases.he: ואמנם כח התבונה שמתפשט ממוח הבינה, היינו מה שביכולתו להביא עצם ההשגה לבחינת התפשטות למטה ממנה בכל ענין נבדל הימנה, או לחיוב או לזכות או להתפעל בלב, וכן להביאה במחשבה בכמה אופנים שונים כו'.
phrases.en: ]It is[ therefore ]understood that[ the power of *Tvunah*, which spreads forth from the mind of *Binah*, is the ability to bring the essential comprehension, to an aspect of spreading down from it, in all matters that are separate from ]the concept[ itself. ]That is to say, he is capable of arriving at a verdict[ whether for “guilt” or for “innocence” etc. Likewise, the arousal [of the emotions] of the heart [comes from this power]. Furthermore, [he is capable of] bringing it into thought in many various angles.

blocks.text: It follows that **the power of *Tvunah*, which spreads forth from the mind of *Binah*, is the ability to bring the essential comprehension, to an aspect of spreading down from it, in all matters that are separate** from the concept itself: to a verdict of guilt or innocence, or to **the arousal [of the emotions] of the heart**, for he knows that this matter will bring *hispaalus* (emotional arousal).
The words **bringing it into thought in many various angles** open what the book discusses later: the letters of thought come from *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

From the recap at the start of the next class: *tevuna* is the power of *bina* to spread out, to bring the essence of the comprehension downward, into separate things and into the *middos* (emotions).

But *tevuna* can also go up, as *bina* can; it is a full *bina* by itself. The power of *chachma sheb'bina* (discovering a new thing within the same thing, off to the side) originates in *tevuna*, and so does *bina sheb'chachma*, understanding one thing from another. That is why one who has *bina sheb'chachma* is called a *navon*, a man of *tevuna*, and not a *mevin*.

*Chachma sheb'bina* comes specifically from *kelita*, not from *bina*, which only understands the concept itself. This is why the opening definition says only that *tevuna* is the *spreading* of the light of *bina*, not the spreading down: spreading means in every direction.

sections.title: The emotions within bina, and coming to a decision
sections.summary: Bina has emotions of its own, the intellect's leaning toward merit or guilt, but they are still intellect, with always another side. To bring them out into a final decision or ruling takes a man of tevuna, one who has absorbed the matter.

phrases.he: אך לכאורה אנו רואים שיש בבינה עצמה בחינת מדות הנקרא ז׳ תחתונים דבינה, ונקרא מדות שבשכל המטה כלפי זכות או שכל מטה כלפי חוב כידוע
phrases.en: However, at first glance, we see that in *Binah* itself, there exists an aspect of emotions, which are called the seven lower *sefirot* of *Binah*. These are [also] called the emotions of the intellect that leans either towards merit, or the intellect that leans towards guilt, as known.

phrases.he: היינו כמו שהמדות שבשכל הן בעצם ההשגה עדיין בהעלם
phrases.en: However, these are only as the emotions still are concealed within the essential comprehension.

blocks.text: We see that **in *Binah* itself, there exists an aspect of emotions, which are called the seven lower *sefirot* of *Binah*.**

What came before was the *Chabad* (intellect) of *bina*; now he speaks of the seven lower levels of *bina*, the *middos* of *bina*, which are the forty-nine gates. **These are [also] called the emotions of the intellect that leans either towards merit, or the intellect that leans towards guilt**.

When one analyzes something, besides understanding it one also comes to a view that it is a good thing or a bad thing. In studying Chassidus, for example, the analysis leads to the decision that this is good. That is an intellect leaning toward merit, and it is already a *midda*, not the actual understanding of what Chassidus is.
That decision is what will awaken the *daas*, for the thing or against it.
However, **these are only as the emotions still are concealed within the essential comprehension.**
It is not an actual feeling of liking something; it is a mental decision that this seems good and ought to be liked. The *middos* of the intellect are not *middos*; they are intellect.

phrases.he: אבל להביא בחינת התגלותן בדבר נבדל, כמו להורות בענין מקרה דבר מה על פי השכל והסברא הזאת, להטות את המשפט של זה הענין לחסד וגבורה שבו דוקא, הרי איש תבונה דווקא יוציא לאור מן המדות שבבינה כו'
phrases.en: Nonetheless, to bring these emotions out into revelation in a separate matter, such as to shed light upon a certain case according to this concept and reasoning, and to [actually] cause the judgment on this matter to lean either to kindness or sternness, specifically requires a man of *Tvunah*. ]It is specifically a man of *Tvunah*] who can bring out insight and light, from the emotional [*sefirot*] of *Binah*.

blocks.text: Nonetheless, **to bring these emotions out into revelation in a separate matter**, **to [actually] cause the judgment on this matter to lean either to kindness or sternness, specifically requires a man of *Tvunah*.**

blocks.title: On the one hand, on the other hand
blocks.text: In *bina* there are forty-nine *middos*. It is like the man in *Fiddler on the Roof*: on the one hand it is a good thing, but on the other hand, from this *sevara*, it is bad, and on the other hand, from that one, it is good. As long as it is in the intellectual brain of *bina*, there are many other hands.
But to come out with what it finally is: that is already *tevuna*; to arrive at a *psak halacha* (halachic ruling) takes specifically a man of *tevuna*.
Later he explains that the real ruling comes from *daas*, the mind of *hata'a* (inclining): *bina* says this and that, and finally one says, “I have to decide already.”

This, he says, is why women cannot be rabbis or *poskim*, and why they are called *kalei daas*. It is not that they have less *daas* than a man; they have the same amount. But their *bina yeseira* (extra measure of *bina*) unsettles their *daas*: they always come up with another hand, another detail, and cannot stop to make the final decision. They can make decisions, he adds; the point is the pull of the extra *bina*.

sensitivity.reason: Explains why women cannot be rabbis or poskim by their extra bina unsettling their daas.

blocks.text: That is why someone who thinks too much cannot be a good businessman: a time comes when he must decide without knowing all the details, and in *bina* there is always another detail; details are infinite.
Where the reasons all weigh to one side (should I jump from an airplane without a parachute?) no inclining is needed. It is needed where the balance is close and some things cannot be known now.

What makes a great authority like the Rambam or the Rif is that they learned the matter so well that they had *kelita*: not only did they understand it, they absorbed it, and it became part of their brain. Therefore they can arrive at a halachic decision usually out of *tevuna*, without having to resort to a feeling for it.

The basic work of *tevuna* is explanation and application: before, explanation, bringing the water out to the sheep; now, application, whether in halacha or in science, as with the Greeks' steam engine.

phrases.he: ואיש תבונות היינו כח הקולט בכי טוב לעצם ההשגה, על כן מתפשטת ההשגה בו לעשות ולהורות בה כמה ענינים נבדלים לגמרי
phrases.en: The meaning of “a man of *Tvunah*” is that he has a thorough grasp of the essential comprehension. Because of this, the comprehension spreads forth in him, to do and to shed light upon many completely separate matters.

phrases.he: וגם ביכולתו להביא את עומק בינה לידי גילוי כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין
phrases.en: He even is capable of bringing the depth of *Binah* itself into revelation, as explained above. This will suffice those of understanding.

blocks.text: **The meaning of “a man of *Tvunah*” is that he has a thorough grasp of the essential comprehension**: the absorption of the comprehension.

**Because of this, the comprehension spreads forth in him, to do and to shed light upon many completely separate matters.** *Kelita* is the *Keser* (crown) of *tevuna*. It too comes from *hisbonenus*, the double *nun*, going over and over. If one goes over the matter until it is understood and stops there, there is no *kelita*.
**He even is capable of bringing the depth of *Binah* itself into revelation**.

So there are two things, application and explanation. The essence of *tevuna* is *kelita*, and its power is to spread the matter out. Generally, “*tevuna*” means downward: either down into application, or down into explanation to somebody else.

sections.title: Yisroel Saba and Tevuna: emotions of the intellect on their way out
sections.summary: Tevuna is the emotions of bina as they come out of bina, as Yisroel Saba is the emotions of chachma. Its last level, Malchus of tevuna, is the root of the letters of thought: still part of the mind itself, unlike thought, which is already a garment.

phrases.he: (והיינו בחינת אבא ואמא תתאין ישראל סבא ותבונה ישראל סבא מדות דחכמה ותבונה מדות דבינה אך באין בבחינת הגילוי לחוץ ובחינת מלכות דתבונה הוא השכל הבא במחשבה הנקרא אותיות מחשבת שכל שהשכל מתלבש בה והוא בחינת כלי חיצוני למחשבה עיונית שהוא גלוי השגה דבינה עצמה מצד עצם השכל והסברא כו' ומבחינת מלכות דתבונה נמשך שרש אותיות המחשבה עצמה שנקרא לאה כו' והוא ד' רבתי דאחד)
phrases.en: (This then is the aspect of the lower father and mother, *Yisroel Sabba* and *Tvunah*. *Yisroel Sabba* is the aspect of the emotions of *Chochmah*, and *Tvunah* is the aspect of the emotions of *Binah*. However, these two are how these emotions come into revelation, to the outside. The aspect of *Malchut* of *Tvunah* is the aspect of the intellect which comes in thought, which is called the letters of intellectual thought (*Machshevet Sechel*), within which the intellect becomes invested. It is the external vessel for analytical thought (*Machshava Iyunit*), which is the revelation of the comprehension of *Binah* itself, from the aspect of the essence of the concept and explanation. From the aspect of *Malchut* of *Tvunah* is drawn the source of the letters of thought themselves, which is called *Leah*. This (*Malchut* of *Tvunah*) is the aspect of the large *Dalet* (ד) of the word *Echad*-אחד.)

blocks.text: **This then is the aspect of the lower father and mother, *Yisroel Sabba* and *Tvunah*. *Yisroel Sabba* is the aspect of the emotions of *Chochmah*, and *Tvunah* is the aspect of the emotions of *Binah*.**
Yet they are not simply the *middos* of *chachma* and of *bina*: **these two are how these emotions come into revelation, to the outside.**

As just explained, the *middos* of *bina* are not *tevuna*; one can have them and be unable to apply them. The *middos* of *bina* as they stay inside are just that; *tevuna* is those *middos* as they come out of *bina*. It is the *middos*, not the intellect of *bina*: the *Chabad* of *bina*, its actual *hisbonenus*, stays entirely within itself.
Even so, though *Yisroel Saba* and *Tevuna* are only the *middos* of *chachma* and *bina*, each becomes a full *partzuf* (configuration) of ten *sefiros*, so *tevuna* too has its own *Chabad*.

**The aspect of *Malchut* of *Tvunah* is the aspect of the intellect which comes in thought, which is called the letters of intellectual thought (*Machshevet Sechel*)**: thought as it still is within the intellect. Later it will be explained as *Leah*.

**It is the external vessel for analytical thought (*Machshava Iyunit*)**. Analytical thought is the actual *iyun* (analysis) taking place inside the intellect, and it is clothed in the *machsheves sechel*, the actual letters. The distinction is very fine: there is no analytical thought without the external letters. The letters come specifically from *Malchus* of *tevuna*, because it takes the inner analysis and puts it into a separate thing: letters, words and concepts.

One might ask: is *Malchus* of *tevuna* then not *Leah* itself, only its root? It is still part of the essence of the intellect, as it is coming out. *Leah*, in terms of the worlds, is already like *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*: actual thought, speech and action. Thought is no longer part of the essence; it is a *levush* (garment). *Malchus* of *tevuna* is still part of the body, the actual inner intellect.

blocks.title: Speech over the telephone
blocks.text: Right now we are talking. The letters of speech are a wholly separate garment, nothing but sounds: over the telephone they are turned into pulses of electricity, then back into movements of air, then into signals along the listener's nerves. My speech came from my thought, which is letters too and not really part of me, only a more inward garment, in my brain, put on and taken off. *Malchus* of *tevuna* is still part of the brain itself; *Leah* is already like talking inside one's head.
All this is explained much later in the book; here it is only introduced. *Malchus* of *tevuna* **is the aspect of the large *Dalet* (ד) of the word *Echad*-אחד**.

sections.title: Ben u'vas: tevuna, the lower mother of the emotions
sections.summary: Tevuna has its own depth, length and width: its depth is kelita, its length is bringing the concept into teaching or action, its width is widening it in thought. It is the lower mother that gives birth to the emotions; bina is only their grandmother.

phrases.he: וזהו שנקרא תבונה בן ובת כידוע, להיות כי גם בתבונה יש ג' דברים, עומק ואורך ורוחב. העומק הוא עצם כח התבונה הזאת שבאותה ההשגה, כמו שהיא בשעה שקולטת אותה כו'
phrases.en: For this reason, *Tvunah* is also called *Ben U’Bat* – Son and Daughter, as known. This is because *Tvunah* likewise possesses the three [dimensions of] depth, length and width. Its depth is the essential strength of the power of *Tvunah* of this comprehension, as it is during the time which he grasps it.

phrases.he: ובה יוכל עומק ההשגה הנזכר לעיל לבוא לגלוי, כנזכר לעיל בפסוק איש תבונה ידלנה כו'
phrases.en: Through this (grasp) he is capable of bringing the [very] depths of the concept [out] into revelation, as was previously explained on the verse, “a man of *Tvunah* shall draw them (the deep waters) out.”

blocks.text: **For this reason, *Tvunah* is also called *Ben U’Bat* – Son and Daughter, as known.**
The letters of תבונה, rearranged, spell בן ובת. *Ben u'vas* means *chesed* and *gevura*, that is, *daas*: as explained later, the mind of *daas* divides into two *mochin*, *chesed* and *gevura*.

So *tevuna* is where *daas* comes from; bringing the matter into an actual feeling of *middos* comes specifically from *tevuna*. It is the actual mother of the children, the lower mother. *Bina* does not bring the children directly, only through the lower mother.

**This is because *Tvunah* likewise possesses the three [dimensions of] depth, length and width. Its depth is the essential strength of the power of *Tvunah* of this comprehension, as it is during the time which he grasps it**: the actual *kelita*.
*Kelita* takes the thing in by absorption, not only grabbing it and holding on. Holding on is from the outside; *kelita* is absorbing it like a sponge, so that it becomes part of oneself.

**Through this (grasp) he is capable of bringing the [very] depths of the concept [out] into revelation**: specifically through this *kelita*, the depth of the concept comes out, as in the verse **“a man of *Tvunah* shall draw them (the deep waters) out.”**

phrases.he: והאורך הוא ירידתה בענין אחר הנבדל, להורות בו ולעשות מעשים רבים על ידה כו'
phrases.en: The length of *Tvunah* is the descent [of the concept] into a separate matter, to shed light upon it, or to accomplish many actions through it.

blocks.text: **The length of *Tvunah* is the descent [of the concept] into a separate matter, to shed light upon it, or to accomplish many actions through it**: bringing it down into a separate thing, either to teach and explain it to somebody else, or to apply it in actual action.

phrases.he: והרוחב הוא בחינת התפשטות התבונה בעצם ההשגה, להרחיבה במחשבה בכמה רבוי אופנים שונים ולא כמו שהיא לבד כו'
phrases.en: Its width is the aspect of the spreading forth of his *Tvunah* in the essential comprehension [itself], to expand it in his thought in many different manners, and not just [in the essential manner] that it is.

blocks.text: **Its width is the aspect of the spreading forth of his *Tvunah* in the essential comprehension [itself], to expand it in his thought in many different manners**.
This means the width of *bina* really comes from the width of *tevuna*: only with *kelita* can there be real expansion within *bina* itself.

He adds one more thing, mentioned before though not here: since *bina* has a height, so does *tevuna*. From the power of *kelita* one comes to understand one thing from another, and only one who has absorbed the matter can do so. That is why he is called a *navon*: the root of *navon* is *tevuna*, not *mevin*. A *navon* is a master of *tevuna*.

phrases.he: ומה שכלולה התבונה מב''ן וב''ת, היינו מה שמתבונה דוקא יולדו המדות בגלוי מהות בפני עצמם, כי מבינה עצמה לא היו תולדות המדות אף על פי שנקרא אם הבנים כו' (אבל היא אימא עילאה)
phrases.en: ]Now, the reason] that *Tvunah* is called *Ben U’Bat* – Son and Daughter, is because it is specifically *Tvunah* that gives birth to revealed emotions as matters in and of themselves. For although *Binah* is called the “mother of the children,” nonetheless, from *Binah* itself, there is no birth of the emotions (since it is the “upper mother”).
notes: See Etz Chayim (Shaar Av”I) Shaar 14, chapter 8.

blocks.text: The reason is that **it is specifically *Tvunah* that gives birth to revealed emotions as matters in and of themselves**, *chesed* and *gevura*, through the mind of *daas*.
Yet **from *Binah* itself, there is no birth of the emotions**, because *bina* remains entirely intellectual: there is always another hand, another analysis.
This is so **although *Binah* is called the “mother of the children,”** since without the original *hisbonenus* there would be no *tevuna* either.
*Bina* is **the “upper mother”**: in a way, the grandmother, the original source but not the immediate one.

It could be called the *savta* (grandmother), as *Yisroel Saba* is called the grandfather. *Bina* is not the mother of the *middos*; it is the mother of *tevuna*, the mother of the mother of the *middos*. That is, it is the mother of its own *middos*, and those *middos* of *bina*, when they come out, are *tevuna*.

*Bina* is the mother of *tevuna*; *tevuna* is the mother of the emotions.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן התבונה נקרא אימא תתאה להוליד המדות, והוא בחינת ב''ן וב''ת, אהבה ויראה, שבאים בהתכללות בתבונה דוקא, שהיא בחינת התפשטות אור הבינה למטה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: In contrast, *Tvunah* is called the “lower mother,” [for it is she] who gives birth to the emotions. These [emotions] are the aspects of “Son and Daughter” – love and fear, which specifically come about included in *Tvunah*. [This is because *Tvunah*] is the aspect of the spreading forth of the light of *Binah* downward, as explained above.

blocks.text: **In contrast, *Tvunah* is called the “lower mother,”** which gives birth to the *middos*: **love and fear, which specifically come about included in *Tvunah*.**

Only in *tevuna* do all the “other hands” come together in *hiskalelus* (inclusion) to bring out the actual, final *midda*. In *bina* it is all still in little pieces, a piece here and a piece there; putting the pieces together into an actual product happens only in *tevuna*.

It is **the aspect of the spreading forth of the light of *Binah* downward**. At the start of the chapter he did not say “downward”; now he defines it more precisely: what is generally called *tevuna* means specifically downward, the lower mother.

The real power of *tevuna*, spreading, goes in other directions too, but those have other names: *chachma* of *bina*, *bina* of *chachma*, and so on. And just as *chachma* and *bina* have a source in the hidden *chachma* and *bina* of *Arich*, *tevuna* also has a source in the hidden *tevuna* of *Arich*: since *bina* includes both *bina* and *tevuna*, so does the *bina* of *Arich*.

sections.title: The intellect of the emotions comes from tevuna
sections.summary: The intellect that lives inside the emotions comes from tevuna, which carries the emotions of bina into the heart. That is the purpose of contemplation: not to be a maskil with a fine idea, but an oved whose feelings are moved.

phrases.he: וגם לזה הטעם בחינת המוחין שבמדות נמשך מבחינת התבונה (וכמו שכתוב יהו״ה בחכמה יסד ארץ, דאבא יסד ברתא כו'
phrases.en: It is also for this reason that the aspect of the intellect of the emotions is drawn from the aspect of *Tvunah*. (This is as stated, “*HaShem*-יהו״ה founded the earth with *Chochmah*, [and established the heavens with *Tvunah*.” The first part of this verse, “*HaShem-*יהו״ה founded the earth with *Chochmah*,” refers to the fact] that “the father founded the daughter.”

phrases.he: כונן שמים בתבונה, שמים הן בחינת המדות, אש מים כידוע
phrases.en: [The second part of the verse states], “He established the heavens with *Tvunah*.” As known, the “heavens-*Shamayim-*שמים” refers to the aspect of the emotions, fire-*Eish-*אש and water*-Mayim-*מים.
notes: See tractate Chagiga 12a. There it states that the Hebrew word for “heaven – *Shamayim*” (שמים) is a conglomeration of two words, *Esh* (אש) and *Mayim* (מים), which mean fire and water. Firstly, these two elements correspond to *Chessed –* kindness, and *Gevurah* – might. Secondly, as will be explained later, the actual makeup of the emotions is from these two elements. Thirdly, it is the emotions which influence the speech and action, and therefore, the emotions (*Zeir Anpin*) are called “heaven” while speech and action (*Malchut*) which receives from the emotions, is called “earth.”

blocks.text: **It is also for this reason that the aspect of the intellect of the emotions is drawn from the aspect of *Tvunah*.**
The *mochin* (intellect) of the *middos*, the *mochin* of *Zeir Anpin*, come from *tevuna*, not from *bina*.
As the verse says, G-d founded the earth with *chachma*: “**the father founded the daughter**,” *Malchus* comes from *chachma*.
“**He established the heavens with *Tvunah***”: with *tevuna*, not with *bina*.
As known, **the “heavens-Shamayim-שמים” refers to the aspect of the emotions**, fire and water, *chesed* and *gevura*.

phrases.he: וכן ובתבונה יתכונן, שהוא בחינת קיום המדות בבחינת המוחין דתבונה שבהם, כי התבונה כמו ממוצע להביא מוחין מבחינת מדות דבינה במדות שבלב
phrases.en: Similarly, [it is stated], “They are established with *Tvunah*.” This refers to the establishment of the emotions [because] of the aspect of the intellect of *Tvunah* which is in them, since the aspect of *Tvunah* is like an intermediary to bring the intellect from the aspect of the emotions of *Binah* into the emotions of the heart.

blocks.text: **This refers to the establishment of the emotions [because] of the aspect of the intellect of *Tvunah* which is in them**: the *mochin* of the *middos* come specifically from *tevuna*, **since the aspect of *Tvunah* is like an intermediary to bring the intellect from the aspect of the emotions of *Binah* into the emotions of the heart.**
The *mochin* of the *middos* come from the *middos* of the *mochin*, the *middos* of *bina*; but to become the *mochin* of the *middos*, they must pass through *tevuna*.
This is what is called the *uvchein*, the “and therefore.”

The *mochin* of the *middos* are an *uvchein*: not the essence of the intellect, the *Chabad* of *bina*, only the *middos* of *bina*. That is why in *avodas halev* (the service of the heart), when the matter is brought down into the heart, only its end passes through, the *uvchein*, and not the intellect itself; whereas in *avodas hamochin* (the service of the mind) the whole *Chabad* of *bina* comes into it.

phrases.he: שזהו כמו כח ההבאה בענין הנבדל, שהוא עיקר ענין התבונה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This is similar to the power to bring [a concept] into a separate matter, which is the principal aspect of *Tvunah*, as explained above.)

blocks.text: **This is similar to the power to bring [a concept] into a separate matter, which is the principal aspect of *Tvunah***.

Here it means bringing the intellect into a *midda*, since a *midda* is something separate from the intellect. The power of *tevuna* does several things: to teach others, and to apply; and applying includes bringing out the actual *middos*, bringing the intellect into the application of an actual feeling.

From the recap at the start of the next class: the main point of *hisbonenus* is to bring it into the *middos*. That was the whole point of *Kuntres HaHispaalus*: not just to be a *maskil* (one who understands) but an *oved* (one who serves). *Hisbonenus* is *avoda*, not *haskala*, an intellectual exercise. Many people make a big mistake in thinking that those who learn something like *Shaar HaYichud* are *maskilim* with their heads in heaven.
The *hisbonenus* is specifically *tevuna*, because *daas* comes from *tevuna*: *ben u'vas*, the mind of *daas*, which brings about actual *middos*.

As the author writes there, what his father the Alter Rebbe wanted was for Chassidim to have *hispaalus Elokus*. The goal is the *middos*: to get excited, not to sit back and say, “How interesting, so what is *Arich* and what is *Atik*?”

The goal of *avodas halev* is to get fired up. A greater goal is *avodas hamochin*, where the whole mind is fired up and the thought of *bina* itself grows hot. Greater still, up in *Atik* and *Arich*, the *ratzon* (will) and *taanug* (delight) grow hot, so that this is where one's delight comes from.

Higher than that is the essence of the *yechida*: “this is what I am.” It is said of the Mitteler Rebbe that if he were pricked with a needle, Chassidus would come out instead of blood, the blood being the soul.

This is above delight: one who wants something for its delight wants it only while the delight comes. The essence of the soul is willing to give up everything, even its life *al kiddush Hashem*, as even a simple Jew is; and why? Because this is what I really am. These are the five levels of *hispaalus* that he explains there.

sections.title: The two nuns: hisbonenus between bina and tevuna
sections.summary: Bina's bent nun is width and tevuna's straight nun is length. Hisbonenus, bina sheb'bina, joins them: going over the same explanation once more brings kelita, kelita brings tevuna, and tevuna brings daas and the emotions.

phrases.he: וידוע גם כן שיש נו''ן כפופה ונו''ן פשוטה בבינה, להיות נו''ן כפופה הוא הרוחב ונו''ן פשוטה הוא האורך
phrases.en: Furthermore, as known, in *Binah* there is a bent *Nun* (נ) and a straight *Nun* (ן). That is, the bent *Nun* (נ) is the width, while the straight *Nun* (ן) is the length.
notes: See the Magen David of the Radbaz on the letter *Nun*. Also see Pardes Rimonim of the Ramak, *Shaar HaOtiyot* (27:17).

phrases.he: ונ' המלוי שלו בנ' פשוטה מה שאין כן בשאר מילוי האותיות
phrases.en: Furthermore, when expanded, the *Nun* which fills it is the straight *Nun*, which is not the case with the expansion of any other letters.
notes: When one expands the letter *Nun* – נ (as opposed to just *N*) it would be spelled out as - נו"ן. It then includes both the bent *Nun-*נ and the straight *Nun-*ן.

blocks.text: As known, **in *Binah* there is a bent *Nun* (נ) and a straight *Nun* (ן).**
Within *bina* itself there are a bent *nun* and a straight *nun*, and the same within *tevuna*. Taken generally, between the two, *bina* is the bent *nun* and *tevuna* the straight one.
That is, **the bent *Nun* (נ) is the width, while the straight *Nun* (ן) is the length.**

Furthermore, **when expanded, the *Nun* which fills it is the straight *Nun***: the *milui* (spelling out) of the letter is נו״ן, a bent *nun*, a *vav*, and a straight *nun*, **which is not the case with the expansion of any other letters.**

One might ask: the letter *mem* also ends with a *mem*, and *vav* with a *vav*. With *mem*, the open and the closed *mem* are two levels of the same thing. What is special in *nun* is that its *milui* is a *nun*, a *vav* (“and”) and a *nun*. The *vav* both separates them and unites them: “and” means there are two things, and that they are connected. So in *bina* there are two separate matters, not just two levels: *bina* and *tevuna*.

phrases.he: כי האורך נכלל ברוחב וכך הוא בתבונה, ואמנם נון הכפל בענין הנקרא התבוננות, כמו עמי לא התבונן וכו', שזהו בחינת פנימית בינה הנקרא עיון, לעמוד על דבר כו'
phrases.en: This is because the length is included in the width. This is likewise the case with *Tvunah*. However, in regard to the double *Nun* in the matter which is called *Hitbonenut* (התבוננות), as in the verse, “My nation does not contemplate – עמי לא התנונן”; this is the inner aspect of *Binah*, which is called *Iyun*, to stand upon the subject etc.

blocks.text: **This is because the length is included in the width**: the expansion of the length is included in the width. If one has the width of the whole explanation in his head, he can bring it down and explain it to others; without the width, he cannot.
**This is likewise the case with *Tvunah***: it too has a length and a width.
As for **the double *Nun* in the matter which is called *Hitbonenut***, **this is the inner aspect of *Binah*, which is called *Iyun*, to stand upon the subject**, over and over again.

phrases.he: שנקרא בינה שבבינה, הוא ממוצע בין בינה לתבונה על ידי הנו''ן פשוטה, שמחמתו נקרא התבוננות כו' ודי למבין:
phrases.en: This is called *Binah* of *Binah* and is an intermediary between *Binah* and *Tvunah*, through the aspect of the straight *Nun*. For this reason it is called *Hitbonenut*. This will suffice those of understanding.

blocks.text: **This is called *Binah* of *Binah* and is an intermediary between *Binah* and *Tvunah*, through the aspect of the straight *Nun*.**

As said before, it is specifically *bina sheb'bina* that brings about the *kelita*. How does one get from *bina* to *tevuna*? Through *hisbonenus*, the intermediary between them. One has grasped the idea with *bina*; how does he come to the *tevuna* of it, to apply it to outside things and teach it to others? Through *bina sheb'bina*, because *bina sheb'bina* brings about *kelita*. There is no separate power of *kelita*.

So *bina sheb'bina* is the main power of all the powers, the linchpin; and it is the one in one's own hands. The other powers are not really in one's hands. Even *daas*, which is partly in one's hands (one can force himself to concentrate), really comes from *bina sheb'bina*.
It works **through the aspect of the straight *Nun***, the length of *bina*: *hisbonenus* within *bina* is the straight *nun*.

*Chachma* of *bina*, coming up with new things, is the width. *Kelita* comes not from new things but from going over the same explanation once more, along the same length. “Fine, we understood it, now let us learn another *Bava*” is width, and it will not bring *kelita*. As any college student knows, to absorb the material one has to read it again.

So far, then: the first chapter explained how *bina sheb'bina* activates all the powers above it, and explained *daas* separately without saying how it is activated. Now he has explained that *daas*, *ben u'vas*, is activated specifically from *tevuna*, and *tevuna* from *bina sheb'bina*, going over the length one more time.

This also explains the Tanya's difference between one who serves G-d and one who does not, between learning a matter a hundred times and a hundred and one times. The hundred times were to understand it; that makes a *maskil*. The hundred and first, once it is already understood, is where *kelita* begins: it brings *daas* into the matter and moves the *middos*, and that makes an *oved*.

reviewQuestions.question: How does *tevuna* come about, and why does understanding a matter well not yet give it?
In the analogy of the deep well, what does the man of *bina* do, and what does the man of *tevuna* do?
What does the example of the Greeks and the Americans show about *bina* without *tevuna*?
Why can someone who understands every *sevara* in a Talmudic debate still be unable to rule guilty or innocent?
Why is *tevuna* called the lower mother, and *bina* in a way only the grandmother?
How does *bina sheb'bina* bring a person from *bina* to *tevuna*, and what does this have to do with learning a matter a hundred and one times?

notes.text: after defining bina as width and tevuna as length he adds a remark on 'the secret of the two Leviathans' (the straight and the crooked nun, the male and female serpents) and why specifically tevuna remained (018 9:13–10:56). The thread is hard to follow in the transcript and it is left out; worth listening to.
his remark about women, bina yeseira and daas (019 7:38–8:42) is included at the editor's request, reported as he said it. Please check the wording against the audio.
the point about 'shasak Rav' (Rav ruling without giving his reason, from chachma inclined in the mind of daas, 019 11:21–12:01) is reported briefly; the transcript is thin there.
he says he does not remember the rest of the verse 'ובתבונה יתכונן' (019 28:18); nothing from that remark is used.

the last three paragraphs come from the opening of tape 020 (0:07–4:31), his recap of this line, cited as such. One phrase, 'like דוד is doing' (020 1:54), is unclear (King David, or someone present?) and is left out.

two digressions are left out of the draft: on meditation practices of idolaters, and on the shevira (breaking of the vessels) having its root in bina sheb'bina and in the 'uvchein', the decision drawn from an analysis, illustrated by a political example (020 9:35–13:15).
the source span runs to the end of tape 020; from 17:04 on it is a separate Talmudic Q&A after the class, not used.
